workflow_steps.name: Architectural Framework Selection
workflow_steps.description: Select the architectural framework appropriate for the system being modeled
workflow_steps.rationale: Different systems (engineered, biological, social, ecological) require different architectural frameworks. UAF 1.2 is ideal for engineered systems, but biological systems benefit from Systems Biology frameworks, social systems from SNA, etc.

user_prompt.question: Which architectural framework best describes your system?
user_prompt.guidance: Choose based on the primary nature of your system

uaf.best_for: Engineered systems: software services, hardware systems, enterprise architecture, defense systems (DoDAF/MODAF)
uaf.examples: Microservices architecture, IoT systems, enterprise IT, system-of-systems integration

systems_biology.best_for: Biological systems: gene networks, metabolic pathways, protein interactions, ecological food webs
systems_biology.examples: Gene regulatory networks, metabolic pathway modeling, protein-protein interactions, ecosystem dynamics

social_network.best_for: Social systems: organizations, communities, influence networks, collaboration networks
social_network.examples: Organizational structure, social media networks, team collaboration, community analysis

ecological.best_for: Ecosystems: food webs, species interactions, population dynamics, conservation planning
ecological.examples: Food web modeling, predator-prey dynamics, ecosystem resilience, biodiversity analysis

complex_adaptive.best_for: Emergent, self-organizing systems: markets, cities, hybrid systems with feedback and adaptation
complex_adaptive.examples: Economic markets, urban systems, traffic flow, multi-agent simulations

custom.best_for: Novel or hybrid systems not covered by existing frameworks
custom.examples: Cyber-physical-social systems, experimental domains, unique research areas

user_prompt.help_text: This determines terminology, templates, and validation rules. All frameworks use the same core abstraction (nodes + edges) and can be analyzed with networkx graph tools.

actions.note: If custom framework selected, LLM researches domain and creates custom definitions file

actions.description: If custom framework: LLM research and definition creation

research_steps: 1. Ask user to describe the system domain and key entities
2. Research domain literature (web search for 5-10 min)
3. Identify common modeling approaches for this domain
4. Create architectural_definitions_custom.json following pattern of other frameworks
6. User reviews and approves generated framework
research_areas: Standard modeling approaches for this domain
Common terminology (what are the 'nodes'? what are the 'edges'?)
Validation criteria specific to this domain
Quality attributes relevant to this system type

notes: All frameworks map to the same core abstraction (nodes with functions + edges with interactions)
Framework choice affects terminology and templates but not core workflow structure
Tools like system_of_systems_graph.py work across all frameworks via framework adapters
UAF 1.2 is default and recommended for most engineered systems

benefits: Automatic context injection based on workflow state
Systematic enforcement of critical behavioral rules
Token-efficient context retrieval (2000-8000 tokens vs 5000-10000 manual)
Prevents LLM agents from forgetting workflow instructions

on_user_query - Semantic search across all knowledge bases

system_isolation_breach - Detects wrong directory or cross-system access

actions.description: Configure automatic git commits (OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED)
actions.purpose: Enable automatic version control commits at key workflow milestones

user_prompt.ask: Would you like to enable automatic git commits during workflow execution?
options: Yes - Enable automatic git commits and pushes (recommended for version control)
benefits: Automatic backup of architecture and code
Meaningful commit messages at logical checkpoints

outcomes.success: Git repo already exists, skip initialization
outcomes.failure: No git repo, proceed with initialization

git_setup.condition: Only if step 1 failed (no existing repo)

user_questions.question: What is your git remote repository URL?
Which branch should automatic commits push to?
Who should be credited as author for automatic commits?

git_setup.action: Create initial git commit for setup
commands:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Initial setup: Directory structure and foundational documents

- Created directory structure (context/, specs/, docs/, services/)
- Added foundational documents (SYSTEM_MISSION_STATEMENT.md, USER_SCENARIOS.md, SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md)
- Initialized working_memory.json and workflow tracking
- Configured automatic git commits

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

error_handling.if_push_fails: Warn user but continue - they may need to configure git credentials or set up SSH keys
error_handling.credential_help:
For HTTPS: git config --global credential.helper store
For SSH: Set up SSH keys with ssh-keygen and add to GitHub/GitLab

git_setup.action: Create git commit helper function documentation
git_setup.content: Documentation on when automatic commits occur and how to disable if needed

commit_schedule.description: Automatic commits will occur at these workflow milestones
01-systems-engineering: SE-02: After each service architecture completed
SE-06: After system graph generated and validated
03-development: D-03: After each service foundation code completed
D-03: After each service implementation completed and tests pass

if_no.action: Skip git setup, set git_automation_enabled: false in working_memory.json
if_no.note: User will manually manage git commits

llm_agent_instructions: ASK the user via AskUserQuestion tool if they want automatic git commits
If YES: Execute git setup steps 1-8 in order
Collect git remote URL and branch from user
Create meaningful initial commit with workflow metadata
Handle push failures gracefully (warn but continue)
If NO: Set git_automation_enabled: false and skip to next step
success_criteria: If yes: Git repo initialized/configured, initial commit made, working_memory.json updated
If no: Git automation disabled in working_memory.json

critical_reminders: ALWAYS use absolute paths when invoking tools: python3 {reflow_root}/tools/<tool>.py {system_root}
Store all path configuration in context/working_memory.json for future reference
Verify reflow_root contains required directories before proceeding
Never assume system is located in reflow/systems/ - it can be anywhere
Use workflow_driver.py to track progress through setup steps
common_mistakes: Using relative paths for tool invocation (causes 'file not found' errors)
Skipping foundational documents (causes issues in later workflows)
Not initializing working_memory.json with path configuration
